scored.historians_note:
─────────────────────────────────────────  
Historians debate the extent to which the Mughal ruling class retained nomadic versus sedentary characteristics, a factor that influences interpretations of their administrative flexibility and openness to foreign technology.  Modern scholars such as André Wink and Jos J. L. Gommans argue for a fundamentally nomadic origin, while Pius Malekandathil emphasizes a gradual sedentarisation [EVIDENCE: mughal_empire_36]. This debate is relevant because a more sedentary, bureaucratically sophisticated Mughal state would be better positioned to organise state‑led industrial projects, whereas a strongly nomadic elite might resist such settled economic transformations.
